author: hoeschec
text:
In reference to my post above (Post # 2007)

Something I noticed about that USD-CAD Short:

There were two scales involved with this trade. The First scale has a UFL and LFL and FO, and the lower scale has the same structure: UFL, LFL, and FO. The reasons I call it the "second scale" is because it forms as a result of it's reaction to the first scale.

What ends up forming, are two FO's.

Not sure how useful this is in trading these zones, but it might be a good idea to find multiple scale FO's occurring in close proximity together, because it decreases the likelihood that price will FO above your entry (If the space above your entry is just a higher TF scale with its own FO).

author: hoeschec
text:
Great entry, but I still got stopped out on this EUR-USD Simulation.

It's a good reminder to be reasonable about targets. In this case, I kept my SL very tight, but my target was too wide. If I widened my SL to just above the FO, my original TG would have been hit nicely.

My Lesson:

If you take a trade with a very tight SL, make sure your target is reasonable (specifically, make sure your TG is placed at the first possible place where price might encounter resistance.). If you want a wider target, keep in mind that your SL may need to be widened to give price a little breathing room.

Same Chart, but with more labels:

A quick reminder that the ideal bullish FO has price making lower lows while ranging above. Vice-versa for bearish FO's.

author: hoeschec
text:
Reasons why this FO did not work:

1. The FL that price Fakes out was not formed as the result of an engulf of something important

2. Price did not make lower lows prior to the FO occurring, which means fewer sellers would be committing to the short. which means fewer traders panic and go long when the see the bullish FO.

text:
OK, I am changing this trade up a bit.

Moving SL to the the CP below in the HTF FL. An entry order is placed near this zone in case we get a spike down to PCP. If price engulfs in to the CP I will get out.

Chart below showing changes to the trade setup.

LTF chart chowing adjustments to entry order and SL.

The nice thing about a trade like this: If I am wrong and price EG in to the CP I have a choice to accept the loss and allow price to hit my SL, or I can eliminate the SL and carefully watch price after the EG occurs...price almost always makes a RT after engulfing in to a compression zone, allowing me to get all or part of my losses back.
